ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The diagram shows a shape made from ten squares of side-length $1 \mathrm{~cm}$, joined edge to edge. What is the length of its perimeter, in centimetres? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is made by joining 10 small squares with the same side length. It can be seen as having a row of 6 unit squares arranged horizontally in the middle; above each of the two rightmost squares, 1 square is stacked, forming an upper group of 2; below each of the two middle squares, 1 square is hanging, forming a lower group of 2. Reasoning: The side length of each small square is 1 cm. If the 10 squares are separated, the total number of sides is 10 × 4 = 40. Now count adjacent shared sides: the horizontally adjacent shared sides include 5 in the middle long row, 1 in the upper group, and 1 in the lower group, for a total of 7; the vertically adjacent shared sides include 2 between the upper two squares and the long row, and 2 between the lower two squares and the long row, for a total of 4. The total number of shared sides is 7 + 4 = 11. Each shared side removes 2 unit sides from the outer perimeter, so the perimeter is 40 - 2 × 11 = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: Use an internal-edge subtraction count. From the image, read the polyomino as a horizontal row of 6 unit squares, with 2 extra squares stacked above the rightmost two squares and 2 extra squares hanging below the two central squares, for 10 squares total. From the text, each square has side length 1 cm. Start with 10 separate squares giving 40 unit edges. Count shared edges visible from the arrangement: horizontal shared edges are 5 in the long row, 1 in the top pair, and 1 in the bottom pair, for 7; vertical shared edges are 2 between the top pair and the long row plus 2 between the bottom pair and the long row, for 4. Total shared edges = 11. Each shared edge removes 2 boundary edges, so the perimeter is 40 - 2*11 = 18 cm.
